observed_behavior: Linux Candidate publication replaces a competing empty final registry directory created at the commit boundary and returns success, while Windows rejects the same destination.
expected_behavior: Windows and Linux publish sealed Candidate directories with an atomic create-only primitive; an occupied final name yields CANDIDATE_EXISTS and preserves the existing entry.
impact: Independent concurrent registry state can be lost, invalidating immutable Candidate identity and cross-platform delivery evidence.

reproduction.symptom_oracle: A final Candidate directory created after the last safety check remains the same inode and sealing fails with CANDIDATE_EXISTS.
steps: Prepare a valid staged Candidate in an isolated host-temp registry.
Create the same final Candidate directory immediately before the directory publish call.
Run the Windows POSIX-semantics regression and the same governance test on native Linux under WSL.
reproduction.sample: Before the fix, both 15-test runs had exactly one failure: KnowledgeError was not raised; the reviewer Linux probe reported competitor_preserved=false and result=returned.

root_cause.summary: The final staged Candidate directory is published with os.replace, whose POSIX semantics permit replacing an existing empty directory instead of enforcing create-only identity.

next_action: Implementation executor uses Windows no-replace rename and Linux renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE), fails closed when unavailable, then reruns Windows/Linux governance and full verification before a new fresh preliminary review.
